content.comment_body: Can anyone help me figure out what I'm doing incorrectly? I'm struggling to get a current output using [product_name] and an analog output module. According to the documentation, resistance across the output terminals should be less than 5K. I've tested with a variety of resistors up to 1M. However, I consistently measure either 19.7mA or very little current (<0.05mA) through the resistor. The voltage across the terminals appears to react as expected, so I don't believe the module itself is defective. It seems to be a configuration or wiring issue on my end. I've attached my test program and believe the 4-20mA settings and scaling are correct.

Hello [user_name], You can check the manual here: [url] Refer to section 2.3.4 for details on wiring the analog module. For current output, connect I1 and M1 for channel 1, and I2 and M2 for channel 2. Ensure your actuator's resistance does not exceed 250 Ohm. Best regards, [user_name]

Thanks [user_name]. You mentioned wiring I1 and M1 for one channel and I2 and M2 for the other. My module and diagram 2.3.3 display V1+, M1, V2+, and M2; that's what I've been using as outputs. Do I need to connect the PE terminals? Currently, I'm using a 122k resistor, which is greater than 5k, but I'm only reading 0.08mA.

Hello [user_name], Apologies for the confusion. I believe you're working with the analog output module [article_no], which supports only 0-10V output. There is another module [article_no] that can deliver both 0-10V and 0/4-20mA current output. Best regards, [user_name]
Thank you again, [user_name]. You're very knowledgeable! My list doesn't mention the module with [article_no]. I'll make sure to obtain the correct one. Thanks again, and happy new year!

Thank you. It was announced that this module would become available in November 2008. I suggest reaching out to your local [company_name] representative for current availability information. Wishing you a happy new year. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The discussion centers around confusion about an analog output module's capabilities while setting up a 4-20mA test rig. The user was not getting the expected current output due to using a module that only supports voltage output, not current. Similar module names and article numbers contributed to the mix-up and incorrect hardware selection, resulting in difficulties configuring the system as needed.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hoped the analog output module would offer both 0-10V and 4-20mA outputs as indicated by datasheets and product labeling, expecting an easy configuration for current output and accurate guidance regarding wiring and hardware capabilities.
